references.text: Parallel account of the consecration of Aaron and his sons, where Moses applies blood to the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe as described in Exodus 29:20.
The same ritual practice of applying blood to the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe is used in the cleansing of a leper.
Oil is applied to the same body parts as the blood in the consecration ritual, showing the connection between cleansing and consecration.
Repeats the ritual with blood on the right earlobe, thumb, and big toe in connection with the cleansing of leprosy.
Oil is applied to the same places as the blood, parallel to the priests' consecration ritual.
Earlier in the same chapter, sprinkling of blood around the altar is described, the same practice repeated in verse 20.
Basic instruction on sprinkling blood around the altar for burnt offerings.
The book of Hebrews explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
Direct fulfillment: Leviticus 8:24 describes Moses' performance of exactly the consecration ritual prescribed in Exodus 29:20.
